answer.rationale: The binding constraint is delivery risk: the line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer and the contract expires in 14 days without auto-renewal. That rules out switch_primary_vendor (memory_c2 explicitly records the low-cost vendor missing SLA in three of four quarters and warns against sole-sourcing them on a critical line) and rules out defer_decision (memory_c5's deferral worked only because that renewal was non-critical and the service continued month-to-month; neither condition holds here). add_second_source (memory_c3) is the right long-run structural move but consumes the single decision slot without addressing the expiring contract or the 18% mandate, and qualifying a new source cannot plausibly land inside 14 days. That leaves renew_incumbent versus negotiate_terms; both preserve continuity (memory_c1), but only negotiation attacks the cost mandate, and memory_c4 plus memory_c6 together suggest the incumbent moves on price and payment terms under market benchmarking and will trade volume pricing for a longer term without narrowing service scope. I verified c4 and c6 because they are the two memories actually load-bearing for the chosen action, and both are the kind of claim most likely to have been flattened in consolidation: c4 does not say how much margin was recovered, and c6 does not say what the multi-year term or the volume floor were. If the recovered savings were only a few percent, negotiation alone will not reach 18% and the honest output becomes a partial cut plus an escalation, not a solved mandate. Uncertainty I am deliberately not collapsing: whether the incumbent concedes enough this cycle, and whether last year's leverage conditions still hold at day 71. Downstream value risk: the 18% mandate creates real pressure to read c2's cost win as licence to switch primary supply, which would trade a hard cost target against an unbuffered line; and a multi-year commitment taken purely for volume pricing can foreclose the second-source move c3 vindicated, so any term I sign should preserve the right to add a qualified second source rather than lock it out.
